brand.name: Shenava Session
brand.description: A recorded consultation becomes a transcript, a dialogue with the two speakers told apart, and a draft of the proposal that meeting should produce — in Persian and English at once.

landing.title: A recorded consultation becomes the proposal it should produce.
landing.lede: Drop in an hour of audio. Shenava Session writes down the words, tells the two speakers apart, and drafts the proposal under the template's headings — in Persian and English at once. Then it stops and waits for you.
landing.passesTitle: Three passes, each useless without the one before it

pass1.title: The words
pass1.body: Your browser cuts the recording into pieces and sends them one at a time. Each piece is saved the moment it comes back, so a closed tab halfway through an hour loses nothing.

pass2.title: Who said it
pass2.body: A model decides which sentences are the consultant's and which are the client's. It answers with sentence ranges and never rewrites anything, so a wrong answer is only ever a wrong label.

pass3.title: The draft
pass3.body: A model reads the labelled dialogue and writes the proposal as finished sentences, in both languages. It is told never to invent a price, a date or a number — what the meeting left open becomes a question.

landing.modesTitle: Two ways of cutting the audio
landing.modesLede: A transcription request is capped at about 2 MiB. An hour of speech does not fit, so the recording is cut — and how it is cut decides how long you wait.

modeMinute.title: Minute pieces
modeMinute.b: Cut at the quietest moment in the 20 seconds before each minute
modeMinute.c: About 60 requests for an hour of audio

modeLong.title: Long pieces
modeLong.a: 9 minutes per piece, Opus at 24 kbit/s, compressed in your browser
modeLong.b: 1.6 MB per piece — under the cap one raw minute nearly fills
modeLong.c: 6 or 7 requests for an hour of audio

landing.privacyBody: Not in the database, not in object storage, not on disk. Your browser cuts the file locally and uploads one piece at a time to a function that transcribes it and forgets it. The text is kept, deliberately, because the text is the product.
landing.costBody: A few cents to transcribe, fifteen to twenty to draft. Every call is checked against a daily and a monthly ceiling and refused before it is sent if it would go over.
landing.sampleTitle: There is a worked example inside
landing.sampleBody: The seed file ships one complete meeting — transcript, dialogue and draft — so a fresh clone shows the whole product before you have set a single key.

dash.title: Meetings
dash.emptyHint: Run db/02_seed.sql and one worked example appears here.
dash.notReady: The database is not connected yet.
dash.notReadyHint: Open Connections and Shenava Session will tell you exactly what is missing.

conn.title: Connections
conn.lede: Three things have to answer before Shenava Session can do anything. Nothing here shows a key's value — only whether it has one.
conn.supabaseWhat: Where the meetings, the transcripts and the drafts live.
conn.openrouterWhat: One key for every model — the transcriber and the writer both go through it.
conn.tablesHow: Open your Supabase project, go to SQL Editor, and run db/01_schema.sql and then db/02_seed.sql.
conn.howBody: Copy .env.example to .env.local and put your values there. The file explains each one. Restart the dev server afterwards — Next.js reads the environment at start.
conn.doorOpen: APP_PASSWORD is empty, so there is no login. That is right on your own machine.
conn.doorClosed: APP_PASSWORD is set, so the dashboard asks for it.
conn.doorWarn: Set it before you put this on a public domain: a public deployment carries your OpenRouter key, and anyone who opens the record page is spending your money.

new.heading: New meeting
new.lede: Choose a recording. Your browser decodes it, cuts it, and shows you the plan before anything is uploaded — the file itself never leaves this page.
new.title: Title

minute.title: Minute pieces (for short consultations)
minute.body: 60 seconds each, uncompressed. About 60 requests for an hour of audio, and 12 to 15 minutes of waiting. Right for a short recording.

long.title: Long pieces (faster, and for long consultations)
long.body: 9 minutes each, compressed in your browser to Opus. Six or seven requests for an hour of audio, and four or five minutes of waiting. Right for a real meeting.
long.unavailable: This browser has no Opus encoder, so it cannot compress the pieces. Safari is the usual case — Chrome or Firefox can.
long.insecure: This address is not secure (http over the network), and the browser only hands out its Opus encoder on a secure page — https, or localhost. The same browser can on localhost; being Chrome is not enough.

new.fileNote: Any format your browser can play. Up to three hours. Nothing is uploaded when you choose it.
new.tooLong: That recording is longer than three hours, which is more than the browser can hold decoded. Split it in two and make two meetings.
new.undecodable: Your browser could not decode that file. Try exporting it as WAV, MP3 or M4A.
new.planLine: {duration} minutes of audio becomes {pieces} pieces, sent one after another — about {minutes} minutes of waiting.
new.planBytes: The file is {mb} MB. It stays on this machine; only the pieces are sent, and only as they are needed.
new.sending: Sent {done} of {total} pieces. One at a time; leave this tab open.
new.sendingNote: The recording is still in this page's memory, so you do not have to choose it again.

meeting.resumeBody: {pending} of {total} pieces are still to send. The audio was never stored — not here, not in the database, not anywhere — so choose the same file again and Shenava Session carries on from where it stopped. It checks the file's fingerprint before sending a single byte.
meeting.sending: Sent {done} of {total}. One piece at a time; leave this tab open.
meeting.mismatch: That is a different recording. The fingerprint does not match the one this meeting was planned from, and sending it would fill the waiting pieces with the wrong seconds. Choose the original file, or delete this meeting and start again.
meeting.replanned: That file cuts into a different number of pieces than this meeting was planned with. It is probably a re-export rather than the original. Delete this meeting and create it again from the file you have.
meeting.undecodable: Your browser could not decode that file.
meeting.sendFailed: The sending stopped partway. Nothing was lost — the pieces that arrived are written down, and choosing the file again carries on from there.

dialogue.heading: Who said it
dialogue.runNote: One model call over the whole transcript at once, not per piece — labels decided piece by piece disagree at the boundaries. The model answers with sentence numbers and never rewrites a word, so the worst it can get wrong is a label.
dialogue.swapWhy: For a pass that had the two people the wrong way round from the start. Moves the whole meeting.
dialogue.moveWhole: Moves this turn and nothing else. No model is called.
dialogue.splitWhy: The usual miss is a one-word answer swallowed by the turn around it. Open the turn and move just that sentence.
dialogue.splitHint: Press a sentence to move it to {side}. What comes before and after keeps this turn's side.

reason.over_ceiling: That would take today or this month past its spending ceiling, so it was refused before it was sent. Raise the ceiling on the Settings page, or wait.
reason.no_transcript: There is no transcript yet. Send the pieces first.
reason.no_database: The database is not connected. Open Connections.
reason.unreadable: The model's answer could not be read as the shape asked for, twice. Try again; if it keeps happening, the writer model on the Settings page may not be one that returns reliable JSON.
reason.transport: The model could not be reached. Check the OpenRouter key and its remaining credit on the Connections page.

draft.heading: The proposal draft
draft.drawNote: One call, both languages at once, under the template's headings. The model writes down the facts first — who said what, every number and date — and then writes both editions from that list and from nothing else. It is told never to invent a price, a date or a number: what the meeting left open becomes a question instead.
draft.drawWithoutDialogue: The speakers have not been told apart yet, so the draft will be written from the raw transcript. It still works, but four of the sections read the client's own lines and the consultant's separately — running the speaker pass first makes a noticeably better draft.
draft.waits: The draft waits for you. Edit a section by typing, have one written again with an instruction, or redraw the whole thing. Every change sets it back to waiting, so nothing you have not read can be approved.
draft.oneLine: One sentence per line. Blank lines are dropped.
draft.prose: Prose, as it will be printed.
draft.emptySection: The meeting did not settle this. Left empty on purpose.
draft.instructionHint: What to change — "shorter", "lead with the bot", "they are a clinic, not a shop"
draft.redrawHint: An instruction for the whole draft, or leave it empty
draft.proposed: This is what it would write. Nothing is saved until you accept it.
draft.wontPrint: Empty, so it will not print
draft.phaseLine: One phase a line: title | when | detail. Then a blank line and the schedule note.

reason.invalid: The request was not in the shape expected.
reason.no_database: The database is not connected. Open Connections.
reason.no_transcript: There is no transcript yet. Send the pieces first.
reason.no_dialogue: The two speakers have not been told apart yet. Run that pass first.
reason.over_ceiling: That would take today or this month past its spending ceiling, so it was refused before it was sent. Raise the ceiling on the Settings page, or wait.
reason.no_key: The OpenRouter key is empty. Open Connections.
reason.unreadable: Twice in a row the model answered, but the answer could not be read as the shape asked for. Try again; if it keeps happening, the writer model on the Settings page may not be one that returns reliable JSON.
reason.transport: No answer came back from the model — not a bad one, none. A 429 beside this line means OpenRouter was busy, and pressing once more is usually enough. If it keeps happening, check the OpenRouter key and its remaining credit on the Connections page.

pour.heading: Into a proposal
pour.lede: The draft's sections are the template's own keys, so pouring is a copy and not a translation of one shape into another. The template decides which sections your proposals print, under what headings, and the lines they always end with.
pour.noTemplates: There are no templates. Run db/02_seed.sql for the built-in one, or make your own on the Templates page.
pour.pour: Pour the draft into this template
pour.approveFirst: Approve the draft first — this is the one gate between a model's sentences and a document with a number on it.
pour.documentsNote: Word is a file; the printer icon opens an A4 sheet with the print dialog already up, so "Save as PDF" is one press. There is no server-side PDF on purpose — a Persian PDF rendered without a real browser gets the shaping and the bidi wrong in ways that look fine in English.
pour.printTitle: Open as an A4 sheet to print or save as PDF

reason.not approved: The draft has not been approved yet.
reason.no draft: There is no draft to pour.
reason.no database: The database is not connected. Open Connections.

templates.heading: Proposal templates
templates.lede: A template is the shape of the document a draft is poured into: which sections you print, under what headings, and the lines every proposal of yours ends with. Two studios reading the same meeting should get the same draft and different documents.
templates.none: There are no templates yet. Run db/02_seed.sql in your Supabase project's SQL Editor and the built-in one appears here.
templates.engagementNote: The meeting page suggests the template whose engagement matches the draft's. Leave it as "not settled" for a general-purpose template.
templates.houseLines: The lines every proposal ends with
templates.houseLinesNote: Your terms, your validity period, your bank details — whatever a proposal of yours always carries. They matter more than they look: the writer is TOLD about these lines so it never proposes them itself, which is why they belong here and not in the draft.
templates.oneLine: One line per line. Blank lines are dropped.
templates.sectionsNote: This list is both what gets printed and **what the model is asked for**. A section you add here is written the next time you redraw a draft. The order is the document's order.
templates.noSections: This template names no sections, so it falls back to the built-in twelve. Add one to shape your own document.
templates.briefHint: For example: the risks the meeting named, one per line. If the meeting named none, leave it empty.
templates.briefNote: This sentence is what the model reads for this section. The more exactly you say what you want and what you do not, the better the section. The rule against inventing a figure is fixed and cannot be changed from here.
templates.optional: Drop it when the meeting left it empty
templates.thenRedraw: Saved. To have the new sections written, open that meeting and press “Draw the whole draft again” — or ask for one section on its own.

settings.heading: Settings
settings.lede: Two seats spend money here, and they want different models: the transcriber turns audio into words and wants something fast and multimodal; the writer reads the whole meeting and wants judgement. One shared model setting would force one of them to be wrong.
settings.noDatabase: The database is not connected, so these are the built-in defaults and saving will be refused. Open Connections to see what is missing.
settings.studioNote: The draft is written against these. They are the reason this project is forkable: your proposals sound like your studio without anyone editing a prompt in the source. Left empty, the draft writes "we" and never invents a name.
settings.transcriberNote: Billed per piece of audio. A meeting in the long cutting mode is six or seven calls; in the minute mode it is about sixty. The recording cap, the prompt, the retry policy and the timeout curve are not settings — they come from @mazarix/voice-kernel, so that this app and anything else built on the same kernel cannot drift apart.
settings.writerNote: Two calls per meeting at most: once to tell the speakers apart, once to draft. This is the pass that needs judgement, so it is worth a better model — and the whole meeting costs cents either way.
settings.ceilingsNote: Read BEFORE every call, and a call that would go over is refused before it is sent. A limit enforced afterwards is a report, not a limit. The figures come from the ledger, so a meeting redrawn next month does not count against last month.
settings.retention: How long a meeting is kept
settings.retentionNote: The audio was never stored. This is about the text — the transcript, the dialogue and the draft — which is kept because it is the product. The clear-out runs when you call shenava_clear_out(), or on a schedule if you set one up with pg_cron.

field.studioVoice: A note on how your studio writes
field.sttFallbackModel: Second engine, for a refused piece

hint.studioVoice: Words to avoid, how formal to be, anything a colleague would tell a new writer. It goes into the prompt as your studio's own note.
hint.sttFallbackModel: Optional. Used when the first engine's safety filter stops a piece. Leave empty to rely on halving the piece instead.
hint.sttMaxOutputTokens: A floor, not a fixed number — a nine-minute piece is given far more room automatically. A long piece sent under a short ceiling comes back truncated, and a truncated transcript reads like bad audio.
hint.writerTemperature: 0.3 is a good place for this work. Higher invents; lower repeats the transcript back at you.
hint.writerMaxOutputTokens: Also a floor. Two editions of a long meeting plus its fact list is more than any fixed number, so the real ceiling is sized to the material.
hint.zeroMeansNone: Zero means no ceiling at all.
hint.retentionDays: Zero means keep forever, which is the default.

settings.spent: Spent so far: ${today} today, ${month} this month.
settings.unpriced: Not in the price table — calls to this model will be counted as free.
settings.unpricedSaved: Saved, but a model you chose has no price entry, so its spending will read as zero and the ceilings will never notice it. Add it to lib/llm/pricing.ts.

code.invalid_type: is not the kind of value this field takes
code.invalid_value: is not one of the allowed values
code.unrecognized_keys: was sent a key this form does not know
code.invalid_format: is not in the right format
